title: Odisha evacuates about 47,000 as Cyclone Akvan speeds up towards Friday landfall near Gopalpur
dek: The storm is moving north at 12 kmph and will cross the Andhra-Odisha coast around noon on Friday with winds of up to 110 kmph, the IMD says; schools are shut in southern Odisha and north Andhra is on alert.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Odisha has moved about 47,000 people out of vulnerable villages and closed schools across its southern districts as Severe Cyclonic Storm Akvan heads for the coast, with landfall expected around noon on Friday, 20 November, between Narsapur in Andhra Pradesh and Puri in Odisha. The administration put the number evacuated at 46,701 on Thursday morning, a figure that reports said was still rising; Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi told reporters on Wednesday that about 50,000 people had been moved.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) said in its latest bulletin, issued through its Kolkata regional centre at 11.30 am on Thursday, that the storm was moving north at 12 kmph and would cross the north Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and south Odisha coasts "close to east of Gopalpur" with maximum sustained winds of 90-100 kmph gusting to 110 kmph. It is the third cyclone to threaten the same stretch of coast in about four weeks, after Arnab in late October and Murasu at the start of November.

## What happened

At 5.30 am on Thursday the storm lay over the west-central Bay of Bengal, about 530 km south of Gopalpur, 590 km south of Puri and 440 km east-south-east of Narsapur, the IMD said. It had picked up speed overnight, from about 5 kmph on Wednesday night to 12 kmph. The IMD expects it to stay a severe cyclonic storm until it reaches the coast, then weaken quickly inland: to a deep depression, with winds of 50-60 kmph, by Friday evening, and to a well-marked low-pressure area over Odisha and Jharkhand by Saturday morning.

In Odisha, Ganjam district accounts for the largest share of the evacuations, with about 25,000 people moved, according to reports. More than 11,000 people have been identified for relocation in Jagatsinghpur. The state says 448 cyclone shelters are open and more than 3,000 more are being kept ready. Pregnant women, children and elderly people are being moved first, and people in hilly areas have been told to leave because of the risk of landslides, reports said.

Reports differ on how many districts are under the IMD's red warning for extremely heavy rain on Thursday and Friday: some say 11, while the Chief Minister referred to 13. Ganjam, Gajapati, Malkangiri, Koraput, Rayagada, Kalahandi, Kandhamal, Puri, Khurda and Nayagarh are among the districts named. Schools and anganwadi centres are closed from 19 to 21 November in Ganjam, Gajapati, Puri, Jagatsinghpur, Kendrapara and Kandhamal, and the Odisha Staff Selection Board has postponed recruitment examinations.

Fourteen National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) teams and 60 teams of the Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force have been deployed, according to reports. The state has released advance assistance of Rs 1 crore each to the districts expected to be hit and has sent seven IAS officers to oversee relief in vulnerable districts. The Water Resources Department has assigned senior engineers to watch river levels from Friday to Sunday, reports said.

"The state government is fully prepared and has already begun taking measures to address the situation," Majhi told reporters after a review meeting at the Special Relief Commissioner's office on Wednesday. He said avoiding any loss of life was the government's first priority.

In Andhra Pradesh, the state's Real Time Governance Society asked the north coastal districts of Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam, Kakinada and the Godavari districts to stay on alert for the next 24-36 hours, reports said. Fishermen along the Srikakulam coast have pulled their boats ashore as the sea turned rough, and strong waves were reported in Ranasthalam mandal. Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam, Anakapalli, Alluri Sitarama Raju and Kakinada are the districts most at risk of very heavy rain, according to reports.

## Further afield

Three long-distance trains through the region were rescheduled on Thursday: the Charlapalli-Shalimar East Coast Express, the Secunderabad-Howrah Falaknuma Express and the Bengaluru-Muzaffarpur Express, reports said. Passengers have been asked to check train status before travelling.

The storm's northward track also brings it closer to West Bengal. The IMD's Kolkata centre forecasts heavy to very heavy rain of 7-20 cm at one or two places in South 24 Parganas and East Midnapore on Thursday, heavy rain in Kolkata on Thursday and Friday, and has hoisted local cautionary signal No. 3 at the Kolkata and Haldia ports. Fishermen have been told not to go out along the Bengal and Odisha coasts or in the north-west and west-central Bay until Friday.

## Background

Arnab crossed the Andhra Pradesh coast at the end of October, and its remnants caused floods and landslides in southern Odisha: three members of one family were killed in a landslide in Kandhamal and about 60,000 people were moved to safety across nine districts. Murasu crossed the coast near Ongole on 3 November and damaged crops on more than 30,000 hectares in Andhra Pradesh, without loss of life, according to the state government. The IMD has moved Akvan's expected landfall several times this week: from the stretch between Nellore and Visakhapatnam, which it forecast on Tuesday, north to the Narsapur-Puri window on Wednesday.

Odisha has made mass evacuation the centre of its cyclone policy since the 1999 super cyclone, which killed nearly 10,000 people in the state. The forecast landfall area around Gopalpur is in Ganjam, the district that took the brunt of Cyclone Phailin in 2013 and was flooded again by Arnab's remnants last month, so the ground is already saturated in many places.

## What happens next

The IMD issues national bulletins every three hours. Landfall is expected around noon on Friday, after which the storm should weaken over Odisha. The heaviest rain in southern Odisha and north coastal Andhra Pradesh is forecast for Thursday night and Friday, and the storm's remnants are expected to bring rain to Jharkhand, south Bengal and northern Odisha on Friday night and Saturday. The Declaration will update this story after landfall.

## Key numbers

- 46,701: people evacuated in Odisha by Thursday morning, according to the administration
- 448: cyclone shelters open in Odisha; more than 3,000 more on standby
- 90-100 kmph, gusting to 110 kmph: forecast winds at landfall
- 12 kmph: the storm's speed at 5.30 am on Thursday, up from about 5 kmph
- 3: cyclones to threaten the Andhra-Odisha coast since late October
